classification.difficultyReason: Use equal horizontal distances to express two tangent ratios, rearrange for BC, substitute into the supplied preceding result, and subtract the height difference from h. The three show-that parts explicitly guide the symbolic argument.

content.prompt: From an observation tower $AB$, an observer measured angles of depression of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ to the top and bottom, respectively, of another tower $CD$. Let $E$ be the point directly above tower $CD$ such that $CE$ is the same height $h$ as $AB$.

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 2 diagram between the shared stem and part (a)
spec.description: Left tower AB and right tower CD on horizontal BC. E is above D and level with A. Solid AB, BC, CD, AD and AC; dashed AE and ED. Right-angle marks at B and E. Alpha spans AE to AD; beta spans AE to AC. Diagram is unshaded, with ordinary marks and labels black under the house colour policy.
spec.mathematics: AB=CE=h; AE=BC; DE=CE-CD. Alpha is the angle of depression to D and beta is the angle of depression to C. Coordinate choices express the source topology without supplying additional measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: All lines, marks and labels are permanent givens. No response or solution values are shown.

answer.worked:
The opposite sides of rectangle $ABCE$ are equal, so $AE=BC$. In right-angled triangle $AED$,
$$\begin{align*}\tan\alpha&=\frac{DE}{AE}\\DE&=AE\tan\alpha\\DE&=BC\tan\alpha.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: By first finding an expression for $BC$, show that $DE=\dfrac{h\tan\alpha}{\tan\beta}$.

answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $AEC$, $CE=h$ and $AE=BC$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan\beta&=\frac{CE}{AE}\\\tan\beta&=\frac{h}{BC}\\BC&=\frac{h}{\tan\beta}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the result from part (a).
$$\begin{align*}DE&=BC\tan\alpha\\DE&=\frac{h\tan\alpha}{\tan\beta}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Hence, show that tower $CD$ has height
$$h\left(\frac{\tan\beta-\tan\alpha}{\tan\beta}\right).$$
